items.title: CVE-2026-129448: Apache Roller unauthenticated code execution in XML-RPC endpoint (Update: added to CISA KEV)

items.title: CVE-2026-49869: Kestra code execution via auth bypass in AuthenticationFilter (Update: Nuclei template published)
items.summary: Update: Nuclei template published. Kestra, an open-source orchestration platform, has an authentication bypass that lets an attacker create and run arbitrary workflows, giving them remote code execution as root inside the Kestra worker container. It can be reached remotely over the network without logging in, and because the bug is listed in CISA's catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities, attacks are happening.

items.title: CVE-2026-126714: PHP remote code execution via partially written session files (Update: proof of concept on GitHub published)
items.summary: Update: proof of concept on GitHub published. PHP's default file-based session handler can leave a session file with a mix of new and old data if a write is interrupted, so an attacker who can influence session data may inject objects and, if the application contains a suitable gadget chain, run code on the server. The attacker can reach this remotely without logging in, though the attack depends on interrupting a write at the right moment.

items.title: Buffer overflow in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder enables unauthenticated RCE
items.summary: CVE-2026-114938, which the researcher Calif is calling Java4Shell, is a buffer overflow in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. The optimized decoder miscalculates the store mask for the padded tail of its input and writes past the end of the output buffer. The bug lives in the JIT-compiled fast path behind java.util.Base64.Decoder , so any application that decodes attacker-controlled Base64 can reach it. Login headers and file uploads are the obvious entry points. items.title: CVE-2026-129289: PHP request smuggling in FPM via unread request body (Update: proof of concept on GitHub published)
items.summary: Update: proof of concept on GitHub published. PHP (PHP-FPM) can mishandle an unread HTTP request body when an application opens php://input without reading it fully. In setups where the web server reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache, a remote attacker with no login can send one crafted multipart request to forge a backend request and potentially run attacker-controlled PHP code.

items.title: CVE-2026-121481: OpenSSL out-of-bounds write via integer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock (Update: proof of concept on GitHub published)
items.summary: Update: proof of concept on GitHub published. Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() in OpenSSL with an input length close to INT_MAX can overflow the calculation of the encoded output size. This causes writes past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer.

items.title: GPUThor: Amplifying Rowhammer Attacks via Non-Uniform Patterns to Exploit ECC-Protected GPUs
items.summary: arXiv:2609.16546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: GDDR memory in GPUs is vulnerable to Rowhammer attacks, where rapid memory accesses induce bit flips in adjacent cells, enabling data tampering and privilege escalation. However, prior GPU Rowhammer attacks trigger only tens to hundreds of bit flips, orders of magnitude fewer than CPU attacks, severely limiting their practical impact. This gap stems from the reliance of existing GPU Rowhammer attacks on uniform hammering patterns that activate aggressor and decoy rows equally, which results in low hammering intensity for aggressor rows. items.title: NCSC-2026-0509 [1.01] [M/H] Kwetsbaarheden verholpen in PHP

items.title: CVE-2026-133949
items.summary: pip prior to v26.2.2 the certifi bundled with pip contains the compromised eMudhra certificates. Upgrading to a secure version of pip should be done either by first upgrading Python to a version that rejects the compromised intermediates (CVE-2026-115557) or use hash pinning with a known-secure version of pip. See the references below for more information.

items.title: CVE-2026-132661
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), multi-factor authentication (MFA) is not enforced on the PEM web application's own routes. An attacker who knows the password of a user who has enrolled a second factor can skip the second factor and call PEM's pages and APIs directly, with that user's permissions. A similar issue in pgAdmin 4 was assigned CVE-2024-4215. From PEM 10.6.1, every authenticated PEM route requires a completed MFA check.

items.summary: Net::DNS uses a 16-bit query ID to match responses to the corresponding requests. In versions up to and including 1.57, the ID is obtained from Perl's built-in rand() function. An attacker that can observe the sequence of query IDs is able to expose the internal state of the PNRG and hence predict query IDs before they are transmitted. The victim Net::DNS instance is then exposed to forged responses injected by the attacker. Note that the deduplication cache in 1.57 has no impact on the feasibility of this attack.

items.title: CVE-2026-133496
items.summary: A security vulnerability has been detected in Matthias-Wandel jhead up to 3.3. This affects the function RemovePngSectionByType/RemovePngSection of the file src/pngfile.c of the component PNG Section Handler. The manipulation leads to double free. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

items.title: CVE-2026-127057
items.summary: The Danfoss legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800 Series are vulnerable to unauthorized access when default credentials or known passwords are used for authentication. These products were manufactured with default credentials documented in the product manual. All versions are affected.

items.title: CVE-2026-124771
items.summary: Authorization omission in the 'admusers' operation of the POST request to '/xmanagercore/api/services/' in XOneManager 3.8.3.0. The API fails to verify the required role for querying the directory. An authenticated member of the project can obtain the list of platform accounts—including administrative accounts—along with details such as email addresses, roles, and associated companies.

items.title: CVE-2026-124772
items.summary: Authorization bypass in the publication of XOneManager 3.8.3.0 updates. During testing, the server accepted initial requests from an authenticated project member with read-only access without verifying publication permissions. If the workflow is completed, updates with modified content could be distributed to managed devices.

items.title: CVE-2026-124769
items.summary: Authorization omission in the 'users' POST operation at '/xmanagercore/api/services/' in XOneManager 3.8.3.0. The API checks project membership but fails to validate the role required to manage users. An authenticated user can view the list of users in the project, including their internal IDs, first names, and last names.

items.title: CVE-2026-96295
items.summary: Authenticated users can bypass normal controls on the reading and writing of workflow execution results. This allows any authenticated user to read or modify any other user's workflow execution results. This issue affects Apache Texera (incubating): from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue.

items.title: CVE-2026-124770
items.summary: Authorization bypass in the ‘tablesData’ operation of the POST request to ‘/xmanagercore/api/services/’ in XOneManager 3.8.3.0. An authenticated project member can execute SQL queries using ‘filter’ without the server verifying their execution permissions. The queries use the service account’s permissions. During testing, databases outside the project were queried, including the authentication database.

items.title: CVE-2026-99684
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: hwrng: virtio - prevent use-after-free after a failed restore remove_common() frees the driver data during freeze, but does not clear vdev->priv, which points to freed memory. items.title: CVE-2026-99680
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: mark the inode preallocated for pNFS write layouts past EOF xfs_fs_map_blocks() marks the inode XFS_DIFLAG_PREALLOC only when it allocates blocks for a write layout. items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks A client can commit a hole in a LAYOUTCOMMIT, because nfsd does not check the extents against its layouts. xfs_iomap_write_unwritten() then allocates written blocks there. A large hole overruns the block reservation and shuts XFS down. A small one exposes stale data. Refuse such a range with -EIO, using XFS_BMAPI_CONVERT_ONLY.

items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent xfs_iomap_write_direct() reserves blocks for the whole count in an unsigned int. For a pNFS layout the client chooses that count, and an RW LAYOUTGET for 16 TiB wraps the reservation and shuts XFS down. xfs_bmapi_write() maps at most XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN blocks here, so cap the count at that. nfsd asks again for the rest. The other callers get the same mapping as before.

items.title: CVE-2026-99677
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: xfs: clamp the pNFS layout range to the maximum file size xfs_fs_map_blocks() lets two bad layout ranges through. An offset of 2^63 or more is negative and passes "offset > limit". A length above the limit, such as NFS4_UINT64_MAX, wraps "offset > limit - length" and stays unclamped. With NFS4_UINT64_MAX, a read layout is built from an uninitialized mapping. Reject a negative offset and one at the limit, and clamp the length. This needs "xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one extent".

items.title: CVE-2026-99662
items.summary: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast With nr_pages == 0, GUP-fast still enters its page table walk and can write past the caller's page array. Let's just check_shl_overflow() to reject any such overflow with -EOVERFLOW early.

items.title: CVE-2026-133537
items.summary: A flaw was found in Keycloak. When evaluating access permissions, Keycloak Authorization Services improperly matches resource paths containing wildcard file extensions by evaluating only the file extension suffix and ignoring configured path prefixes. An authenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by requesting a restricted resource that shares a file extension with a more permissive resource, leading to an authorization bypass and unintended access to protected data.

items.summary: A flaw was found in cluster-network-operator. The OVN IPsec certificate signer does not verify that the requested certificate Subject and DNS names belong to the requesting node. In certificate authenticated OVN IPsec deployments, this could enable peer impersonation when the attacker can also satisfy the configured peer address check, potentially compromising protected traffic.

items.summary: An uncontrolled recursion vulnerability exists in the LINE iOS app prior to version 26.19.0. items.title: CVE-2026-133225
items.summary: A flaw was found in Keycloak. When processing token requests using the User-Managed Access (UMA) grant, Keycloak fails to verify whether a target client or resource server is enabled before issuing an authorization token. An authenticated remote user can exploit this flaw to obtain valid Requesting Party Tokens (RPTs) for disabled clients, bypassing administrative access controls and permissions restrictions.

items.title: CVE-2026-133224
items.summary: A flaw was found in Keycloak. When an administrator revokes tokens by setting a not-before revocation cutoff, Keycloak fails to enforce this boundary when processing User-Managed Access (UMA) grant requests using ID token claims. An authenticated remote user with an active session can submit a previously revoked ID token to receive a fresh Requesting Party Token (RPT). This flaw allows an attacker to bypass token revocation and retain unauthorized access to protected resources.

items.title: CVE-2025-71473

items.title: CVE-2026-131877
items.summary: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unbounded arc length in OBJECT IDENTIFIER decoding and encoding. The content of an OBJECT IDENTIFIER or RELATIVE-OID element is passed to unpack "w*" on decode, and the arcs of an OID string to pack "w*" on encode. Perl converts each arc to or from its decimal string in time quadratic in the arc's length, and nothing limits that length. An attacker who controls the decoded data, or an OID string passed to encode, can exhaust CPU with a single oversized arc.

items.title: CVE-2026-131868
items.summary: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read and asn_get. The length an element declares in its BER header is passed to sysread as the read size. Perl grows the target buffer to that size before reading, so memory is allocated from the declared length, not from the data received. A 6-byte header can declare a length of up to 4GB. A single header makes the reading process allocate the declared size. Where the allocation fails, perl exits with "Out of memory", which eval cannot catch.

items.title: CVE-2026-126956
items.summary: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding. Any constructed-form string element causes the decoder to recurse on the element's contents. The BER encoding controls nesting depth at four bytes per level, with no bound checked. Perl recursion is heap-allocated, so the process grows without a stack crash. An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a small deeply nested constructed string.

Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the decoded value is nearly all of the input that follows the element. In the constructed form each zero-length segment copies the rest of the input again, so memory grows with the square of the input size. An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a short constructed BIT STRING. The resulting value also contains bytes from…

items.title: CVE-2026-126682
items.summary: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding. The encoder routes any value with abs >= 2**31 to i2osp without validating that it is an integer. A string in exponent notation such as "1e8000" passes that threshold. Math::BigInt expands it to an 8001-digit integer, and i2osp's per-octet conversion loop is quadratic in that size. An attacker who controls encoded INTEGER values can exhaust CPU with a short exponent-notation string.

items.summary: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv. asn_recv peeks the socket in a loop, doubling the buffer size on each pass until a tag and length can be decoded. When asn_decode_length returns no value because the length is absent or incomplete, no exit fires for that case either. MSG_PEEK leaves socket data unconsumed, so each re-peek returns at once while the buffer size doubles. A single t…

items.title: CVE-2026-126540
items.summary: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic bigint loop in os2ip. Every INTEGER or ENUMERATED longer than four content octets reaches os2ip, which iterates over each content octet with $result = ($result * 256) + $octet. Each multiplication operates on a bigint that grows by one octet per step, so decoding an n-octet value takes O(n^2) bigint work. Nothing limits content length before this loop runs. An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a single oversized INTEGER or ENUMERATED value.

items.summary: Summary The optional imdtls input module does not enforce tls.permittedpeer after a successful DTLS handshake when configured with tls.authmode="name" or tls.authmode="fingerprint". After the handshake succeeds, imdtls performs the additional permitted-peer identity check. If that check fails, the module logs a warning but leaves the DTLS session active. The session is subsequently read and received records are passed to the configured ruleset. Recovering from Indirect Branch Obfuscation with Hex-Rays Microcode
items.summary: This article uses samples obfuscated with the Hikari-LLVM19 framework to present a recovery method for AArch64 indirect branch obfuscation. The method is not intended to handle all indirect branches. Different obfuscators may compute target addresses in entirely different ways, so the target resolver still needs to match the specific obfuscation semantics. However, once one or two successors can be reliably identified, the subsequent CFG completion, function range expansion, and microcode rewriting steps can be reused directly.
